request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
There's now an "Export claims as CSV" button (`data-testid="export-claims"`) next to the people export, and it downloads the claims file the request describes. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

- **Contents:** the header `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`, then one line per claim. People come in list order and each person's claims run oldest first. Retired people are included even when "Show retired" is off.
- **Figures:** due and period are worked out the same way the claim rows on screen work them out. So a claim with no number has an empty number, a claim outside any period has an empty period, and a due with no rate shows `n/a`.
- **Format:** quoting and line ends match the people export. I moved the shared CSV writing and download code into one `downloadCsv` helper that both exports now use. The people export's output is unchanged, and the test checks that too.

The change is only in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`, because the screen already has all the data the export needs. Nothing changed on the server or in stored data, and the export writes no audit records.
